questions.q: HDZero is connected to SERIAL3 with two wires. Which pair of parameters starts the OSD in ArduPilot 4.7.2?
questions.explain: DisplayPort is port protocol 42 and backend 5 (MSP_DISPLAYPORT). Backend 5 looks specifically for a port with protocol 42 (AP_OSD_MSP_DisplayPort.cpp); with 32 or 33 it does not start. The 33 + 3 pair is for legacy DJI V1/V2 goggles, and type 1 is the MAX7456 chip.

questions.q: `OSD_SW_METHOD = 1`, screens 1–3 are enabled with the ranges 900–1300, 1300–1700, 1700–2100. The channel is exactly 1700. Which screen is shown?
options: Screen 2: the upper bound is part of the range
The screen is undefined, so the firmware shows screen 1
Screen 3: the lower bound is included, the upper is not
questions.explain: The condition in AP_OSD.cpp is `channel_min <= value && channel_max > value`. 1700 is not less than 1700, so screen 2 does not match and screen 3 does.

questions.q: `OSD_SW_METHOD = 0`, screens 1 and 3 are enabled, screen 1 is shown. The switch is moved 1000 → 2000, then 2000 → 1000. What is on the screen after each flick?
questions.explain: On any channel change of more than 200 µs, method 0 takes the next enabled screen around the circle; the direction does not matter, and disabled screens are skipped: 1 → 3 → 1.

questions.q: In DJI O3 goggles with the Betaflight font you see foreign symbols instead of the ArduPilot OSD icons. What fixes the character table?
questions.explain: Bit 2 (value 4) enables Betaflight character indexes for DisplayPort; the table is selected when the backend starts, so a reboot is needed. Bit 0 is telemetry mode for protocol 33. `OSD_FONT` applies only to MAX7456 and SITL.

questions.q: A layout was made for `OSD1_TXT_RES = 2`. An item is at X = 52, Y = 17. What happens with `OSD1_TXT_RES = 1`?
options: The firmware moves it to column 49
It is off the grid: there are only 50 columns
It is off the grid: there are only 17 rows
It stays visible, the grid is scaled
questions.explain: Grid 1 is 50×18: columns 0–49, rows 0–17. Row 17 is valid, column 52 is not. ArduPilot does not recalculate coordinates or clamp them to the edge.

options: A pre-arm error: the two OSD types are incompatible
DisplayPort replaces MAX7456 and the analog OSD turns off
Two OSDs at once, analog and DisplayPort, with one current screen
Two OSDs at once, each with its own independent screen
questions.explain: MAX7456 is compatible with DisplayPort and MSP (AP_OSD_MAX7456.h). Both backends draw the same current screen, so for different grids you make two screens. Two identical types and the MSP + DisplayPort pair are incompatible.

questions.q: A 6S vehicle with `OSD_W_BATVOLT` left at its default. When does `BAT_VOLT` start flashing?
options: Below 3.6 V per cell, that is, below 21.6 V
Below 10.0 V, that is, in practice never
questions.explain: The default level is 10.0 V for the whole battery; the item flashes while the voltage is below the level. 3.6 V is the default of `OSD_W_AVGCELLV`, for a different item. The OSD level is not tied to the battery failsafe.

questions.q: Legacy DJI V2 goggles without WTFOS, `SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 33`, `OSD_TYPE = 3`. Where does the flight mode text appear?
options: In the FLTMODE item, as on DisplayPort
Nowhere: legacy DJI does not show ArduPilot modes
In the MESSAGE field, which is the craft name on DJI
In the statistics line after disarming
questions.explain: In AP_MSP.cpp the DJI "craft name" field is mapped to `OSDn_MESSAGE`: the mode and messages go there. The FLYMODE widget is hidden and flashes only on a failsafe (AP_MSP_Telem_DJI.cpp).

questions.q: You need the VTX in pit mode on the ground, full power on arming, and pit mode again after disarming. Which `VTX_OPTIONS` value?
questions.explain: Bit 0 is pit mode, bit 1 leaves it on arming, bit 2 enables it when disarmed: 1 + 2 + 4 = 7. With 1 the transmitter stays in pit mode in flight too; 2 without bit 0 enables nothing; with 3 full power stays on after disarming until a reboot.

questions.q: `VTX_POWER = 450`. What power does the firmware set, and how much is that in dBm?
questions.explain: The level table in AP_VideoTX.cpp: 25, 100, 200, 400, 500, 600, 800, 1000 mW; the value is rounded down, to 400 mW. 10 · log₁₀ 400 = 26.0 dBm.
